checks: Checked the oriented shell identity in both signs. The old inball bounds the radial normal projection below, so the surface change of variables gives the inward-speed sign. The endpoint formula also holds for an interval. For equi-Lipschitz kernels the radial endpoint replacement has uniform O(t²) error, followed by L¹ convergence of the bounded radial quotients.

Compact interior marks retain uniform centered balls by support-function convergence. Positivity there bounds the optimizer parameters. The accepted 1/N floor and bounded parameter norms transfer a common positive floor to both bodies and a fixed neighborhood.

For arbitrary convergent marks and a subsequence of moving optimizers, the transferred floor keeps the limit admissible. Testing the limiting old minimizer in the moving problems and passing to the limit identifies the subsequential parameter limit by uniqueness. Continuity of the old optimizer then gives uniform convergence.

The signed objective difference at the moving optimizer is a lower bound on the energy difference, and the difference at the old optimizer is an upper bound. Both have the same continuous coefficient by uniform kernel convergence and the signed shell estimate.

Applying the shell identity to volume and degree-one and degree-two moments gives centroid differentiability. The old centered first moment is zero, so the moving-centroid terms cancel in the centered second moment. The quotient gives (DΣ−J)/M, and positive definiteness gives the norm derivative for every nonzero u.

Independently checked the signs and normalization on [−1+t,2+2t] at y=0. The exact interval energy is 4AB/(A+B) for endpoint distances A and B. Here E(0)=8/3, D=−1, C=8/9 and J=−9/4. Direct differentiation gives E′=−8/9, Σ′=1/2 and f′=−f/3, agreeing with all three formulas.

Verified the raw source digests and checked c6bafe9ff5de0861 §§3–5 (9)–(15) and d750a370b2e831ee §§1–4. The additive radial displacement and the source’s multiplicative displacement agree via s_t=−(R_t−R)/R and n·(X−o)=R n·ω.

dependencies.mapping: Applies separately to each old body and each positive moving convex body at the common interior marks. Its 1/N denominator floor controls both optimizer families and its optimizer smoothness gives the old parameter continuity.

Each old and moving mark is own-interior in a full-dimensional convex body. The fact gives positive attained energy and a unique admissible optimizer, which identifies the limit of the moving parameters.

overlap.comparison: Its accepted proof uses the same signed shell estimate, uniform optimized energy expansion near old body-tied contacts, and covariance norm variation at Γ-unit normals. The accepted theorem is scoped to a body-tied cover. Here the claim is independent of compatibility or old contacts, is uniform on arbitrary compact own-interior sets, and records the full covariance derivative and the energy-only normalization explicitly.
Gives marked energy continuity under positive Hausdorff convergence, including boundary marks. It has neither the signed radial first-order coefficient nor a covariance derivative.
Uses a related radial shape derivative for retained mass, under nested motion and with a hinge kernel. It does not give the optimized projective kernel derivative on signed radial paths.

readability: The positive neighborhood floor concerns the kernels at the old and moving optimizers, which are the only parameters used in the envelope comparison.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The signed radial assumptions give a uniform marked-energy derivative on arbitrary compact interior sets, together with the stated normalized profile and within-fiber covariance derivatives.
